_comment: Master place-art manifest for the BOBR game/explorer (42 real places). Each gets a 64-bit picture of the REAL place. `historical_photo` = a verified public archival image (Library of Congress / Calisphere, no API key) to img2img FROM for period accuracy; places without one need a Google Maps Street View reference (capture via the browser agent, no key). Pipeline: generate.py --place <id> [--ref <photo> --denoise 0.45 --aged] -> verify_place_art.py. Tuning: clear reference + low denoise (~0.42-0.5) = faithful + aged; crop photo borders/captions first. Coordinates from the enumeration agent (a2b50daf); photos from the research agent (a1854f8). Confidence: HIGH lower-Mother-Lode towns, LOW upcountry (West Point/Sandy Gulch/ranch — no period photos, reconstruct from landscape + Maps).

places.name: The Welcome Gate (Back of Beyond Ranch)
places.prompt: a rustic split-rail ranch gate on a dirt lane, golden oak-dotted Sierra foothills, a mountain behind at sunset
places.note: Location 1 of 14. No period photo; reconstruct. Ranch land-history = Harris Ranch (Leif 2026-06-14).

places.name: West Point
places.prompt: a high-pine Gold Country trading-post village, a single dusty Main Street of wood-frame false-front stores, a blacksmith, ponderosa pine and oak
places.note: CHL #268, Kit Carson. LOW confidence — no 1850s photo; wood-frame false-fronts, few/no stone buildings. Use Maps ref for CHL #268 marker.

places.name: Sandy Gulch
places.prompt: an 1849 trading center in oak-grassland gulch terrain, an adobe store, dry-laid stone walls, a milled-lumber barn
places.note: CHL #253. Bardsley Adobe (1853), Harris barn (1850s, milled lumber). No Gold-Rush photo.

places.name: Harris Ranch / Harris Barn
places.address: upper Sandy Gulch, West Point, CA 95255
places.prompt: an 1850s timber-frame barn of locally milled lumber, board siding, gable roof, dry-laid stone footing, oak-grassland and pine
places.note: The documented ranch the BOBR land was carved from (Leif's canon). Barn still stands; no archival photo online.

places.name: Mokelumne Hill
places.prompt: a stone Gold Rush county-seat town on a hill, locally-quarried rhyolite and brick buildings with iron shutters, a tall 3-story stone IOOF Hall, plank sidewalks, dirt street
places.note: True 1866 L&H photos exist (loc.gov/item/2002723067). HABS IOOF Hall.

places.name: Hotel Leger
places.prompt: an 1851 two-story stone hotel block, adjacent stone storefronts, iron shutters, plank sidewalk

places.name: Angels Camp
places.prompt: a single dusty Main Street along a creek gulch, rubble-stone storefronts with iron doors interspersed with wood-frame porched buildings, a two-story stone hotel
places.note: 1857 Kuchel&Dresel lithograph; Angels Hotel HABS (Twain's jumping-frog building, 1855).

places.name: Angels Hotel
places.address: 1287 S Main St, Angels Camp, CA 95222
places.prompt: a two-story stone Gold Rush hotel with iron-shuttered windows and a columned wooden second-floor balcony, dusty main street
places.note: CHL 734. VERIFIED place-accurate img2img at denoise 0.42 (2026-06-15).

places.name: San Andreas
places.prompt: a Mexican-camp main street turned county seat, squat fireproof stone stores and Classical Revival brick fronts, a two-story brick courthouse and jail
places.note: Black Bart tried here 1883. No pre-1900 photo; HABS + 1923 copy. Use Maps for the courthouse (30 N Main).

places.name: Calaveras County Courthouse
places.address: 30 N Main St, San Andreas, CA 95249
places.prompt: an 1867 two-story brick county courthouse with arched windows and a jail wing, where the gentleman bandit faced a judge
places.note: Black Bart trial building, now the museum. Clean Street View match.

places.name: Jackson
places.prompt: a Mother Lode town on a narrow Main Street curving through a ravine, two-story brick blocks with iron shutters and arched windows, raised sidewalks, the great hanging oak
places.note: National Hotel 1862. Hanging tree burned 1862 — no photo, render from description.

places.name: Kennedy Gold Mine
places.prompt: a deep hard-rock gold mine headframe and stamp mill on a hill above town, timber gallows-frame, tailing works
places.note: 5,912 ft shaft. Headframe extant for Maps ref.

places.name: Murphys
places.prompt: a Main Street lined with honey-locust trees, unpaved, board sidewalks, a squat two-story rough-stone hotel with folding iron shutters, single-story stone storefronts
places.note: True 1866 L&H photos. Murphys Hotel 1856. (Fire was 1859, not 1854.)

places.name: Sutter Creek
places.prompt: a single narrow winding Main Street along a creek in a steep ravine, brick and native-stone storefronts with iron doors and cantilevered balconies, stamp mills on the hills
places.note: True 1866 L&H 'Sutter's Creek from the South' (calisphere kt800018x4). Knight Foundry 1873.

places.name: Volcano
places.prompt: a town in a narrow limestone gulch, gray limestone ashlar and brick commercial buildings with heavy iron shutters, a three-story brick hotel with two-tier wood verandas, roofless stone ruins, oak-and-pine hills
places.note: L&H 1860-70 'Main Street from the St. George Hotel' (calisphere kt6k40193z). St George Hotel clean Maps match.

places.name: St. George Hotel
places.prompt: a three-story brick Gold Rush hotel with attic and two tiers of wood verandas, in a limestone gulch town
places.note: 1867 rebuild. HABS ca0051; Street View directly comparable.

places.name: Back of Beyond Ranch
places.prompt: a modest hewn-log and board-and-batten ranch cabin and timber-frame barn on dry-laid stone, split-rail fences, open blue-oak woodland and golden grass meadows grading to ponderosa pine
places.note: The real ranch base camp. No period photo; landscape reconstruction (more open in the 1850s).

places.name: Nevada City
places.prompt: a Northern Mines hillside town, brick storefronts, the National Hotel, a white firehouse with a bell tower, forested ravines
places.note: National Hotel 1856; Firehouse No.1 1861; Nevada Theatre 1865 (Twain lectured).

places.name: Grass Valley
places.prompt: a hard-rock gold-mining town, the Holbrooke Hotel saloon, headframes and a giant Pelton wheel on the hills, brick Main Street
places.note: Empire Mine; North Star Pelton wheel; Holbrooke 1851; Lola Montez house.

places.name: Mariposa
places.prompt: a southern Mother Lode county seat, a white wood-frame 1854 county courthouse with a clock tower, oak hills, gateway to the giant sequoias
places.note: 1854 courthouse — oldest in continuous use in the West.

places.name: Hangtown (Placerville)
places.prompt: a rough 1849 mining camp main street, wood-frame stores and saloons, the notorious hanging tree, muddy street
places.note: El Dorado County. The Hanging Tree (Studebaker, Hangman's Tree saloon).

places.name: Drytown
places.prompt: the oldest town in Amador, a dusty street with many saloons and wood-frame buildings, oak foothills
places.note: 26 saloons in its heyday.

places.name: Chinese Camp
places.prompt: a Chinese mining settlement with a tong temple, ailanthus 'tree of heaven' groves, stone and adobe buildings
places.note: Tong War 1856.

places.name: Moaning Cavern
places.prompt: the mouth of a vast limestone cave chamber, stalactites, a dark vertical shaft lit by a shaft of daylight
places.note: Largest single cave chamber in CA.

places.name: Calaveras Big Trees
places.prompt: a grove of giant sequoias towering over a pine forest, a massive cut stump (the Discovery Tree), filtered sunlight
places.note: Discovery Tree 1852.

places.name: Natural Bridges
places.prompt: limestone arches spanning a clear creek in oak woodland, a swimmable green pool under the bridge
places.note: Limestone arches over Coyote Creek.

places.name: Donner Pass
places.prompt: a high granite Sierra pass with a frozen lake below, snow-laden pines, jagged peaks, a foreboding winter sky
places.note: Donner Party 1846-47.

places.name: Carson Pass
places.prompt: a high alpine pass at 8500 feet, granite domes, wind-bent pines, an emigrant trail winding over the summit
places.note: Blazed by Kit Carson/Fremont 1844.

places.name: Independence, Missouri
places.prompt: the bustling jumping-off town for the overland trails, a courthouse square, ox-drawn covered wagons being outfitted, brick storefronts
places.note: Queen City of the Trails.

places.name: Fort Kearny
places.prompt: a frontier army post of adobe and sod buildings on the flat Platte River plain, a flagpole, emigrant wagons passing
places.note: Est. 1848 on the Platte.

places.name: Sutter's Fort
places.prompt: a large adobe-walled fort with bastions and a central building, oak-savanna plain, the heart of New Helvetia

places.name: Sacramento Embarcadero
places.prompt: a Gold Rush riverfront of tents and hastily-built wood storefronts, sailing ships and riverboats at a muddy embarcadero, crowds of argonauts
places.note: 1849 tent-city waterfront.

places.name: Abandoned Mining Camp
places.prompt: a weathered ghost town of leaning wood-frame buildings, broken windows, sagebrush high desert, a lonely headframe
places.note: Bodie as the archetypal Gold Country ghost town.

places.name: The Hydraulic Scar
places.prompt: a vast hydraulic-mining scar of raw red-and-white eroded cliffs and pinnacles, washed-out hillsides, a few pines clinging on
places.note: Malakoff Diggins-type terrain.
